title: Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) in Wildland Fire Operations
cross_references: NWCG Standards for Fire UAS Operations, PMS 515

nodes.text: Initiate UAS operations in wildland fire

evidence.source_text: Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) in Wildland Fire Operations

nodes.text: Be aware of UAS presence and role in providing aerial support

evidence.source_text: Awareness: Be aware of the presence of UAS in the operational area and their role in providing aerial support to firefighting efforts.

nodes.text: Follow established protocols for interacting with UAS

evidence.source_text: Prioritize safety by following established protocols for interacting with UAS and respecting their operational space.

nodes.text: Ensure UAS operations are authorized and comply with policies and regulations

evidence.source_text: Compliance: All UAS operations must be authorized and comply with agency aviation/UAS policies, Federal carding requirements, and Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) regulations.

nodes.text: Ensure UAS/Remote Pilots possess current FAA Airmen Certificate and agency approved Pilot Card

evidence.source_text: All UAS/Remote Pilots are required to possess current FAA Airmen Certificate and agency approved Pilot Card for the assigned mission.

nodes.text: Establish positive communication on approved FM frequencies before UAS launch

evidence.source_text: Communication: Communications with UAS are conducted on approved FM frequencies, UAS will not launch until positive communication has been established.

nodes.text: Select launch and recovery sites with clear operational view and outside heavily traveled areas

evidence.source_text: Launch and Recovery Sites: Type 3 and 4 UAS can be launched from multiple locations based on mission type. When possible, find sites with a clear operational view and outside of heavily traveled areas.

nodes.text: Consider mission objective, timing, product delivery, and location of line personnel before requesting UAS

evidence.source_text: Prior to requesting UAS consider the following: Mission Objective, Mission Timing, Product Delivery, Location of Line Personnel.

nodes.text: Ensure dedicated firing boss/aerial ignition supervisor for UAS aerial ignitions

evidence.source_text: UAS Aerial Ignitions (Ai): Ai operations require a dedicated firing boss/aerial ignition supervisor to direct UAS ignitions and coordinate with ground resources.

nodes.text: Understand UAS aerial ignition capabilities: flight time, sphere capacity, camera, and visual line of sight requirements

evidence.source_text: UAS Aerial Ignition (Ai) Capabilities: Flight Time, Sphere Capacity, Camera, Within a TFR UAS can fly beyond visual line of sight (BVLOS). Without a TFR UAS need to remain within sight or extended line of site (ELOS).

nodes.text: Refer to additional resources for further information on UAS operations

evidence.source_text: Refer to https://uas.nifc.gov/ and the NWCG Standards for Fire UAS Operations, PMS 515, for further information on UAS operations.
